Subject: US soybean exports 2026/27 — desk number 1,800 mln bu vs USDA 1,720, and the milestones to track

Team,

Bottom line

  • Our number: 1,800 mln bu, vs USDA's 1,720 (Nov WASDE). We put the chance of finishing above USDA at ~76%. This assumes China buys exactly 25 Mt from the US.
  • With China fixed, the open question is how much the rest of the world buys. It is on pace today. The main risk is Brazil selling more to non-China buyers.
  • If we're right, US ending stocks are ~220 mln bu, not 300. USDA has room to raise exports in the coming reports.

How we got there (in short)

  • We used 10 seasons of USDA weekly export sales by destination. For each region, we added what it has already booked to what it normally books from now until August.
  • China is set at 25 Mt (policy, not seasonality). Brazil's competition is measured from 10 seasons of US vs Brazil shipments to the same buyers.
  • Backtested over 10 seasons, this method was within about ±3 Mt of the final number. The simple "share booked by now" multiplier was off by up to ±12 Mt.

How to read it

  • At or above the 1,800 column: our number holds. Clearly above means 1,825+.
  • Between the two columns: ~1,760–1,800.
  • At the USDA column: USDA is right, so move to 1,720.

For 1,800, the rest of world needs roughly 650 kt/week in November, 520 in December–January and 400 in February. The last 4 weeks averaged 689.

  • The US ships ~74% of its year in Sep–Feb; Brazil ships ~73% of its year in Mar–Aug.
  • Outside China, the US still holds ~9 Mt of Mar–Aug business (31% share). That is the volume Brazil can take.

"Brazil +X Mt" means Brazilian exports to non-China buyers X Mt above their 5-yr average of 26.3 Mt.

  • Our 1,800 already allows about 25 mln bu for Brazil competing harder than normal (roughly +2 Mt).
  • If Brazil reaches the provider's forecast of 33.5 Mt to non-China buyers, our number drops to ~1,735, which is about USDA's level. Brazil's line-ups from February are the key check.

Caveats

  • China at 25 Mt is an assumption. Each ±1 Mt changes our number by about ±38 mln bu.
  • Brazil's competition is measured by volume (we have no FOB price spread data yet). Data run through week 9 (29 Oct); we will update weekly.
